### On the current state of Japanese consumer

Japan’s consumer backdrop presents a striking divergence between improving labor fundamentals and deeply defensive household behavior. Labour demand remains robust as acute structural shortages continue to strengthen workers’ bargaining power. Employment rates have taken another leg higher since March 2026, while associated nominal wage gains are increasingly feeding through to household incomes, allowing real (inflation-adjusted) earnings growth to mark consecutive positive months.

However, this improvement in real purchasing power has failed to catalyze a recovery in domestic consumption. Instead, households are directing surplus income into precautionary savings to buffer against the psychological shock of persistent everyday inflation and adapting to the Bank of Japan's rising interest rate environment. 

Consequently, real domestic household spending has contracted for eight consecutive months, registering its sharpest drop in two and a half years. The parallel expansion in headline retail sales does not reflect local demand, but is rather an illusion driven by sticky nominal price increases and unprecedented inbound foreign tourism capitalizing on the weak Yen.This structural fragmentation leaves the broader economic recovery highly vulnerable to external pressures. Key risks remain external geopolitical shocks, particularly those capable of driving oil prices sharply higher while undermining consumer and business confidence, alongside Japan’s already stretched fiscal position.
